note: Twelve items. Score each honestly - a generous score helps nobody. Most first-pass profiles land in the 40s. Limits checked against X's help pages in September 2026: display name 50 characters, username 15, bio 160, header 1500x500, profile photo 400x400.

items.full_marks: The bio's first line says who you help and what changes for them, in plain words. Not a list of titles, not 'passionate about', not a string of emoji.
One checkable piece of proof in the bio: a number, a thing you built, a name people know. One, not four.
A pinned post exists, is one of your best-performing posts or a clear 'start here', and is recent enough that it is still true. A new visitor reads this before any of your other posts.
Your real name, optionally plus one word of what you do. Under 50 characters. No emoji wall, no 'DM for collab'.
Readable, spellable after hearing it once, and the same handle you use elsewhere if you can get it.
Your face, filling most of the circle, readable at 40px in a reply thread. High contrast against the background. Shot in the last two years.
1500x500 with one line of positioning or proof, nothing important in the bottom-left where the profile photo covers it. Not the default grey, not a stock skyline.
The website field goes to the one place you want a new follower to go next, and that page matches the promise in the bio.
Your last 10 posts are recognisably about what the bio says you are about. A visitor who likes one post can predict the next.
The Replies tab shows real replies to other accounts in your niche in the last week. On X, that tab is your networking in public.
Posted in the last three days, and on most weeks for the last month. Not necessarily daily.
The bio sounds like a person. No 'visionary', 'thought leader', 'serial entrepreneur', 'building in public' as the whole identity, no three hashtags.
